title: Impact of Varying BLAS Precision on DCMESH
problem: High computational costs in high-accuracy quantum molecular simulations limit their application to large systems. The work explores reducing these costs through precision variations in BLAS operations while maintaining simulation accuracy.
motivation: Quantum molecular simulations require both significant compute power and memory, restricting their practical application to large systems; reducing these costs while preserving accuracy would expand their utility.
method: The framework (DCMESH, combining divide-and-conquer optimization with Maxwell-Ehrenfest-surface hopping—a technique for simulating quantum molecular dynamics) runs simulations on Intel Data Center GPU Max Series 1550 GPUs. To speed up the calculations, it can use different numerical precisions (BF16, TF32, or Complex 3M) depending on the simulation's needs. The precision level is controlled entirely through environment variables—just a setting you change before running—rather than requiring code edits or recompilation. This makes it simple to deploy and tune across many different simulation jobs without extra engineering work.
key_novelty: Using environment variables to switch BLAS precision enables up to 3.91x faster quantum simulations while keeping the important output values accurate, all without modifying the code.
contributions: Demonstrates 1.35x speedup on single GPU while retaining accuracy in excited electron counts, current density, and kinetic energy
Shows up to 3.91x speedups for individual BLAS calls on large problem sizes
Proves precision mode switching requires only environment variables, eliminating source code modification barriers
Establishes applicability to general HPC workloads with significant BLAS computation

metrics.speedup: 1.35x single GPU stack, up to 3.91x for individual BLAS calls
metrics.accuracy: Retains accuracy in excited electron count, current density, and kinetic energy

primary_theme: Mixed-precision BLAS optimization for quantum simulations
